properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-08, in his words: "does something explain to the agent on certain calls what it is that reflow2 is doing from a systems engineering perspective and that the agent has to do the translation for the user into reflow2 jargon and systems engineering terminology? … At its most basic simplification, reflow2 is simple concept that every system is composed of 'black boxes'… I feel like the agent should be able to take this concept and be able to do the translation for the user into SE terms. However, that being said, maybe the graph should keep a table of terms and what they translate into in reflow2 jargon? Then this is always available to the agent (even between sessions)."

═══ THE FIRST QUESTION IS FACTUAL, AND IT WAS MEASURED 2026-09-08 ═══

**`get_instructions` — 30,523 characters, the payload the server tells every session to call FIRST on any design work — says "black box" ZERO times.** It says "systems engineering" zero times. It mentions `interface` 7 times and `decompos*` twice, always operationally rather than as a frame.

**The concept reaches the agent through exactly ONE tool description out of 177**: `set_capability_signature`, which names "the black-box interface at that tier" and cites `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition`. That is a tool a session may never call.

**And the translate-for-the-user instruction already EXISTS — attached to 2 of 177 tools.** `get_skill` and `list_skills` return a `lens` field telling the agent to speak the reader's domain and never reflow2's, keeping their own field's words. Nothing else carries it. So an agent that never fetches a skill is never told to translate at all.

⭐⭐ AND THE PRINCIPLE IS ALREADY ACCEPTED INTENT, NOT A NEW IDEA. `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` is ACCEPTED, captured 2026-08-07 in Anthony's own words, and its own text records him saying: *"I'm a little surprised that reflow2 does not have this as it was one of the primary things I designed it for."* **He is now asking the same question a second time, a month later.** A requirement that is accepted, load-bearing, and absent from the instruction surface is exactly the shape this project has recorded before as accepted-then-invisible.

═══ SO THE HONEST ANSWER TO THE QUESTION AS ASKED IS: NO ═══

Nothing explains the SE frame to the agent on ordinary calls, and nothing tells it on ordinary calls that translation is its job. Both mechanisms exist in fragments; neither is where the work happens.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

**(a) STATE THE PRINCIPLE WHERE THE AGENT ALREADY READS — put the black-box frame in `get_instructions`.** Cheapest by a wide margin: one edit to a payload every session already fetches, and it makes accepted intent visible for the first time. ⚠️ **THE COUNTER IS THE STRONG ONE AND IT IS MEASURED: the principle does not disambiguate.** `dec:idea-a-users-domain-vocabulary-has-no-route-into-se-vocabulary` recorded a domain noun for which Interface, Capability, Requirement and Flow were ALL defensible. "Everything is a black box with interfaces" does not choose between them — the routing problem survives the principle intact. Stating it would be right and would not, on its own, remove the need for a translator.

**(b) A TERM TABLE IN THE GRAPH — persistent across sessions.** Anthony's own second thought, and it is the same shape as option (c) of `dec:idea-the-routing-table-routes-grammar-not-domain-nouns`, reached independently in the same conversation. That convergence is itself evidence. It also keeps reflow2's refusal to infer intact: the user states the mapping once, the graph holds it, nothing is guessed. ⚠️ Counter one: **a recorded mapping ossifies an early wrong answer.** If a project's first session mis-files its central noun, the table makes that error permanent and invisible to every later session — the opposite of the intended effect, and worse than improvising each time. It would need a way to be revisited, and something that notices when a mapping is load-bearing and never re-examined. ⚠️ Counter two: this is one step from the framework registry that `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` was correctly DROPPED for — cosmetic renaming that gated capability on a self-declared label. **The line that must hold: a term table maps to reflow2's UNCHANGED node types and gates NO computation.**

**(c) EXTEND THE LENS RATHER THAN INVENT A MECHANISM.** The translate-for-the-user instruction is built, tested and attached to two tools. Widening it to the capture tools costs far less than a new surface, and it is the half that tells the agent translation is its JOB. ⚠️ Counter: a lens on every reply is a per-call tax on payload size, and this project has already measured a per-call rollup costing 1.2-1.9 minutes a session before it was removed. It would want to be the constructors only, not everything.

**(d) SE MEANING ON THE TOOL DESCRIPTIONS THEMSELVES.** Some already do this well — `add_environment_rule` explains the difference between a self-imposed Constraint, a chosen DesignRule and a rule the world imposes. ⚠️ Counter: 177 tools, no check that any of them says what it means in SE terms, and a hand-maintained convention across 177 surfaces is precisely the class this project has now met six times in one day.

**(e) DO NOTHING AND TREAT THE TRANSLATOR AS THE ANSWER.** ⚠️ Counter: it leaves the accepted requirement undelivered for a second month, and every user rebuilds the same layer.

═══ WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DECIDABLE ═══

(a) and (c) are cheap and mostly independent of the answer — the principle SHOULD be visible and the agent SHOULD be told translation is its job, whatever else is decided. **(b) is the one that needs evidence, and it is the same evidence the sibling node asks for**: whether term tables from different projects agree. Until that is known, a term table is a mechanism built for a population of one.

⚠️ HONEST LIMIT: the measurement above is of what the SERVER sends. It does not measure what an agent DOES with it. An agent may translate perfectly well from a frame it was never given, because the black-box concept is not exotic — it is standard systems engineering that a competent model already knows. Nobody has tested whether stating it changes any behaviour, and the cheapest version of (a) is worth doing partly BECAUSE it would let that be measured.
properties.name: OPEN — nothing tells the agent the black-box frame at call time: get_instructions never says it, one tool description carries it, and the translate-to-the-user lens is on 2 of 177 tools. State the principle, keep a term table, or both?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: the ideas enter as ideas, nothing is promoted, and the objection sits beside each rather than replacing it.

AN AGENT'S READING, offered as a finding rather than an answer. The question was partly factual and the factual half now has an answer: no, nothing carries the frame at call time, and the two mechanisms that would (the instruction payload and the lens) each carry half of it in the wrong place. That is worth separating from the design question, because it is fixable independently of what anyone decides about term tables.

The sharpest thing to hold onto is the counter to Anthony's own instinct. He is right that the black-box concept is simple enough for an agent to reason from, and that is exactly why stating it will not be sufficient — the measured failure was not an agent that lacked the frame, it was a domain noun with four defensible homes under it. A principle that is true of everything cannot choose between four things that are all consistent with it.

The other thing worth carrying: he has now asked this twice, a month apart, and the requirement was accepted the first time. That is not a new idea being explored; it is accepted intent that never reached the surface where it would act.
